summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style overview of Thailand, a Southeast Asian country formerly known as Siam. It covers its size, population, provinces, capital, and neighboring countries and maritime boundaries. It also notes that despite being nominally a constitutional monarchy and parliamentary democracy, a 2014 coup established a de facto military dictatorship.
one_line: Overview of Thailand, a Southeast Asian kingdom formerly called Siam, covering its geography, population, capital, neighbors and political system.
key_facts: Thailand is officially the Kingdom of Thailand and was formerly known as Siam.
Thailand is a country at the center of the Southeast Asian Indochinese peninsula composed of 76 provinces.
Thailand is the world's 50th largest country by total area.
Thailand is the 21st-most populous country in the world.
The capital and largest city of Thailand is Bangkok, a special administrative area.
Thailand is bordered to the north by Myanmar and Laos.
Thailand is bordered to the east by Laos and Cambodia.
Thailand is bordered to the south by the Gulf of Thailand and Malaysia.
Thailand is bordered to the west by the Andaman Sea and the southern extremity of Myanmar.
Thailand's maritime boundaries include Vietnam in the Gulf of Thailand to the southeast.
Thailand's maritime boundaries include Indonesia and India on the Andaman Sea to the southwest.
Thailand is nominally a constitutional monarchy and parliamentary democracy.
The most recent coup in Thailand, in 2014, established a de facto military dictatorship.
